reason: Stamens or filaments of two lengths in alternation are a set of like parts differing in size; the firm content is FLOPO unequal. The alternation itself (a series position) is not captured by any term and stays in the source words.
Alternisepalous means placed alternately with the sepals, a position relative to another part; the sepal (PO_0009031) is the second term of the relation, so it is pattern 09, not a value class.
A loose simile for long, thick, rope-like liana stems, with no definite shape, texture or twisting quality behind it; too doubtful for a term.

The examples are inflorescences and spikes with both male and female flowers ('androgynes', Carex 'gynaecandrous'), which is FLOPO androgynous; the order of the flowers (female above male) is lost. The orchid sense (stamens fused with the gynoecium) does not occur here; 'inflorespective' is a transcription error.

'Inner' picks out which member of a series (inner stamens, bracts, tunics) the statement is about; it qualifies the bearer, as pattern 04 records, and has no value class yet (as rule C373 'inner tepal' → tepal).
A tardily dehiscent fruit or pod still opens at maturity along a definite line, so FLOPO dehiscent holds; 'late' is a timing cue kept in the source words.
Negation of FLOPO ruminate; the bearer is the endosperm (albumen, PO_0009089) of the seed, as the examples say.
Negation of PATO heart shaped (EXACT synonym cordate); in all examples the quality is of the base of the leaf, petal or bract.
Like 'covered' (C240), the content is in the protecting structure (recurved margin, small scales, protruding cells), not in a quality of the protected part.
A pseudo-umbel is an inflorescence that looks like an umbel without being one, which is exactly FLOPO umbelliform (resembling an umbel).
French form of septicidal; fruits opening along the septa. 'septicides-septifrages' is a two-value compound whose first value maps here.
The senses differ: mericarps hanging from a carpophore (a relation to another part), parts floating in water, and a bare 'stem suspended'. No single quality fits.
A count: four locules (PO_0025263; anther locule PO_0025264 for stamens, plant ovary locule PO_0025266, fruit locule PO_0025270) in the bearer.
PATO decreased width has the RELATED synonym narrow; 'very' is a degree cue kept in the source words.
A particular odour, found in only three statements; PATO odorous is the firm content. A FLOPO class beside sweet-scented could follow if more floras use it.
The examples are mostly 'chair blanchâtre' (whitish flesh); PATO white has the RELATED synonym whitish. The bearer of the flesh examples is the flesh (e.g. mesocarp), not the whole seed or fruit.
Sepals or bracts that look like bracteoles, i.e. small bract-like leaves; FLOPO bract-like is the nearest term. In PO a bracteole is a prophyll, not a bract, so the mapping is broader than the word.
Lichens growing on the bark are other organisms living on the plant, not a quality of the plant; useful as a field note only.
A crown bearing many well-developed leaves is FLOPO leafy; 'densely' is a degree cue.
PATO tangled is 'entwined and difficult to unravel', which fits intertwined stems, plants and stipules.
Spines, seeds or hairs placed without a consistent arrangement match PATO irregular spatial pattern (repeated parts whose relationships lack consistency).

The examples mix senses: pod articles coming apart, a single leaflet set apart from the others, and scattered parenchyma. One reading (solitary, free or scattered) would be wrong for the other examples.
A twining stem is climbing in the FLOPO sense; the twining direction (a real character, e.g. in Dioscorea) is lost and could become a class if more statements appear.
A measurement of PATO ratio (PATO_0001470) with length (PATO_0000122) over width (PATO_0000921), exactly pattern 11.

target: new: colour marks of a second colour
reason: The part has marks of a second colour (brown, purple): PATO multi-colored (PATO_0001533) plus the colour of the marks. A single term cannot hold both, and the shape of the marks (spots, streaks) is not stated.
Negation of PATO notched (for a base, 'non échancré' = not emarginate, a child of notched). 'non ensellé' (not saddle-shaped) is a different word grouped here by mistake.
A compound of two shape values, ovate (FLOPO:0991024) and elliptic, which the continuum pattern records as two values of one statement.
'Few-rayed' (stellate hairs with few arms, heads with few rays) is a vague count of parts, like 'few-flowered'; the counted part depends on the bearer.
Penninervous = with the secondary veins in two rows along the midrib, i.e. FLOPO pinnately veined.
Not clearly visible, as for 'obscure' (C174) and 'indistinct' (C175): PATO inconspicuous.
